raw.description:
Zipliens is a leading lien resolution company that specializes in streamlining the lien resolution process for personal injury law firms. We are looking for proactive, results-driven individuals to join our dynamic team.

We are seeking a VP of Customer Support to build Zipliens' support function from the ground up. Reporting to the Chief Customer Officer and sitting within the Customer Experience department alongside the VP of Customer Success, this role owns inbound, reactive support for the firms that use Zipliens, along with the operating foundation that makes that support consistent, measurable, and able to scale.

Owning Customer Support at Zipliens is a greenfield opportunity. HubSpot is our core platform for the foreseeable future, and you will design and configure omnichannel support within it, integrating other channels and tools as needed. You will start as a hands-on individual contributor: setting the vision and strategy, configuring the systems, defining reporting standards, and proposing the team and organization build-out as volume and complexity warrant.

Our primary customers are law firm users. Over time, you will also help design a client support experience for claimants that strengthens our value to the firms we serve and helps them deliver better outcomes for their own clients, where that support is desired. You will partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Engineering, Lien Resolution Operations, Finance, Sales, and Marketing.

In your first year, you will focus on:

  • Defining the support strategy and operating model: tiers, scope, channels, hours of coverage, and what Support does and does not own, including triage-level services questions.
  • Standing up omnichannel intake in HubSpot, starting with form submissions, adding chat as an option, integrating phone into the same system, and recommending whether and when to add social channels.
  • Establishing Tier 3 service levels with Engineering and Product, including severity definitions, handoff criteria, and a shared escalation process.
  • Setting reporting standards and a baseline for first response, resolution time, backlog, customer satisfaction, contact reasons, and cost to serve.
  • Building an AI-forward support model that combines a knowledge base, self-service, deflection, triage, and agent assist, with human review where accuracy matters.
  • Proposing the team and organization build-out, including roles, hiring sequence, and capacity model tied to volume data.
  • Evaluating an enterprise or white-glove support tier using cost-to-serve and segmentation data and market research, and bringing a recommendation to the relevant executives.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Support Strategy & Function Leadership

  • Function Ownership: Own the support vision, strategy, and outcomes, translating company priorities into support goals and an operating plan.
  • Hands-On Execution: Work the queue and configure systems directly in the first phase while the function is being built, and move to leading through others as the team is approved and hired.
  • Org Design & Capacity Planning: Propose the team structure, role definitions, hiring sequence, and capacity model, and build a team with clear career paths once approved.
  • Operating Cadence: Run a regular rhythm of metrics reviews and reporting to the CCO and executive team.

Omnichannel Operations & Systems

  • Data Integration & Tooling: Define requirements and establish data flows (such as syncing portal data, case status, CSM data, and customer context) to ensure support agents have seamless visibility into customer history and operational data.
  • HubSpot Ownership: Own the configuration and reporting of support in HubSpot, including ticketing, routing, deflection, service levels, utilization of the knowledge base, and automation, so the data is trustworthy enough to make decisions on.
  • Channel Strategy: Define how customers reach Support across form submissions, chat, phone, and social, and sequence the rollout of each channel.
  • Voice Support: Integrate phone into HubSpot and define coverage, voicemail handling, and staffing so that no call or message depends on a single person.
  • Documentation: Create and maintain support playbooks, SOPs, macros, and internal help content as living assets with named owners and a review cadence; partner with Enablement on knowledge base content and strategy.

Service Levels, Escalation & Quality

  • Tiering & Triage: Own Tier 1/1.5/2 technical support and define what is resolved in Support, what is routed elsewhere, and what triage-level services support looks like for now.
  • Tier 3 Service Levels: Agree on response and resolution targets with Engineering and Product for Tier 3 issues.
  • Quality Standards: Set quality, coaching, and customer satisfaction standards for the function and report against them.
  • Incident Communication: Partner with Product and Engineering on customer communication during incidents and known issues.

Customer Experience & Insight

  • Firm Users: Design the support experience around firm users, who are our primary customers.
  • Claimant Experience: Help define a client support experience for claimants that supports firms in delivering better client outcomes, for firms that choose it.
  • Enterprise Support Model: Use cost-to-serve, segmentation data, and market research to propose and develop an enterprise or white-glove service level with the CFO, CEO, and CCO.
  • Voice of Customer Input: Provide contact-reason data and support trends to the Voice of Customer program and to Product prioritization.

AI & Automation

  • AI-Forward Support Model: Identify and implement where AI improves resolution time, consistency, and cost to serve, such as triage, deflection, knowledge base creation, and agent assist, and define where human review is required.
  • Measurement: Track the effect of automation on quality, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve, and adjust accordingly.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Customer Success: Partner with the VP of Customer Success as well as Lien Resolution Operations to ensure customers move between Support, ops, and account management without repeating themselves.
  • Product & Engineering: Partner on bug triage, Tier 3 service levels, release readiness, and defect trends.
  • Lien Resolution Operations: Partner on routing services questions and aligning customer-facing commitments with operational execution.
  • Finance: Partner on cost-to-serve analysis, headcount modeling, and the business case for any new service level.
  • Sales & Marketing: Partner on help center content, release communication, and customer-facing materials.
  • Integration Partners: Partner with our integration partners on API support and on service level commitments for mutual customers, including how issues are triaged and handed off when they span both platforms.

Qualifications:

  • 7+ years in customer support, technical support, or support operations within B2B SaaS or tech-enabled services, including 3+ years in a leadership role.
  • Experience building or materially rebuilding a support function, including tiers, service levels, routing, knowledge base, quality assurance, and reporting.
  • Hands-on experience configuring a support platform. HubSpot experience is strongly preferred; experience with comparable tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, or Salesforce Service Cloud is acceptable.
  • Experience implementing omnichannel intake, including integrating phone and chat with a ticketing system.
  • Comfort operating as both an individual contributor and a leader: able to work the queue and configure systems while designing the organization.
  • Experience defining and reporting support metrics such as first response, resolution time, backlog, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve.
  • Experience aligning on escalation service levels with engineering or product teams.
  • Practical experience applying AI in support, such as triage, deflection, knowledge generation, or agent assist.
  • Strong analytical and written communication skills, including the ability to build a business case and present it to executives.
  • Experience in legal services, personal injury, litigation-adjacent technology, or a related professional services industry is preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree required. Focus in business, law, or a related field is preferred.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%, primarily for company offsites and support industry events.

Benefits

  • Private Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Company HSA contributions for HDHP participants
  • Flexible Spending Accounts (Health & Dependent Care)
  • Company-Paid Short-Term Disability Coverage
  • Voluntary Long-Term Disability, Life, AD&D, and Supplemental Coverage Options
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick Time & Select Holidays)
  • Paid Parental Leave

Pay Disclosure: The total base salary range for this role is $179,500 - $243,000 annually, with the opportunity for a discretionary bonus. Final compensation will be determined based on skills and experience.

Work Authorization: Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer-sponsored visa support now or in the future.

raw.description:
About High Scale

We’re High Scale — a future-focused, data-obsessed agency revolutionizing video advertising on TV and social media. Think Amazon’s obsession with customer experience meets SpaceX’s fearless ambition—that’s the DNA behind everything we do.

Our 160-person team of creatives, strategists, and innovators produces thousands of high-impact campaigns weekly for the world’s leading lifestyle, fashion, beauty, and DTC brands. With 50,000 sq. ft. of DTLA studios and a global influencer network, we’re ready to 10x our output in 2026—and we need a Social Media Manager who can build, engage, and grow our brand presence across all digital channels.

Why This Role Matters

Brand perception, community engagement, and cultural relevance are your playground. As the Social Media Manager, you are the voice and pulse of High Scale's brand. You’ll be the bridge between our agency's groundbreaking work and the wider industry, translating our internal innovation into a compelling public narrative. You’ll manage our social channels, build an engaged community, and ensure our brand feels like a VIP in every digital interaction.

Your work will directly impact our brand authority, inbound leads, and our reputation as industry leaders. If you thrive on building communities and telling powerful brand stories, this is your launchpad.

What You’ll Do

  1. Own Our Social Channels

    • Develop and execute a comprehensive social media strategy for High Scale's brand (LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, etc.).

    • Create, curate, and post engaging content daily that showcases our work, culture, and expertise.

    • Manage the content calendar, ensuring a consistent and high-quality brand presence.

  2. Build & Engage Our Community

    • Serve as the primary voice of the brand, actively responding to comments, DMs, and mentions.

    • Proactively engage with industry leaders, potential clients, and creative partners to build relationships.

    • Develop and implement strategies to grow our follower base and increase engagement rates.

  3. Coordinate Content Creation

    • Work closely with our internal creative, production, and marketing teams to source and repackage campaign highlights, case studies, and behind-the-scenes content.

    • Translate complex agency wins and data into simple, shareable, and impactful social posts.

  4. Represent the Brand & Analyze Trends

    • Act as an ambassador for High Scale, embodying our innovative and data-obsessed culture.

    • Provide insights on industry trends, platform changes, and competitor activity.

    • Track and report on key social media KPIs, using data to refine and optimize your strategy.

Who You Are

  1. A B2B & Creative Storyteller

    • 3–6 years of experience in social media management, preferably for a creative agency, media company, or tech brand.

    • Proven track record of growing and managing professional social media accounts, especially on LinkedIn and Instagram.

  2. Organized & Strategic

    • You can juggle multiple platforms, content formats, and priorities without breaking a sweat.

    • Skilled at building content calendars, managing assets, and coordinating with multiple stakeholders.

  3. Excellent Communicator

    • Clear, confident, and persuasive in both written and verbal communication (English fluency required; Spanish is a major plus).

    • You have a sharp, witty, and professional writing style adaptable to different platforms.

  4. Collaborative & Adaptable

    • Thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments.

    • Able to work with creative, production, and leadership teams to execute ambitious brand goals.

  5. Data-Driven

    • Track KPIs (engagement, reach, follower growth, leads) to inform decisions and strategy.

    • Comfortable using social media management and analytics tools to report on performance efficiently.

Perks & Benefits

  • Growth Opportunities: Influence the growth of High Scale's brand and collaborate on top-tier campaigns for global brands.

  • Relentless Innovation Culture: Move fast, test constantly, and collaborate with some of the most creative minds in social media and video production.

High Scale is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and believe it’s key to building teams that change the world—one breakthrough campaign at a time.

About SPERTON

SPERTON is a global recruitment and consulting company with more than 20 years of experience and operations across Europe, Asia and the Americas. We support our clients with Executive Search, Recruitment and Contract Staffing across Engineering, Energy, Infrastructure, IT and Commercial functions.

As part of our continued growth in Sweden, we are looking for an experienced Senior Recruiter to join our team and help build the next chapter of SPERTON Sweden.

The Role

Initially, the role will focus primarily on recruitment delivery and consultant hiring, taking ownership of the full recruitment process from requirement gathering to successful placement.

For the right person, the role can naturally evolve into a broader 360 Recruiter / Business Development Manager position after approximately 3-6 months, including client acquisition, account development and commercial responsibility.

This is an excellent opportunity for an entrepreneurial recruiter who wants the freedom to work remotely and the opportunity to significantly influence their own earnings.

Key Responsibilities

Recruitment Delivery

  • Manage end-to-end recruitment and consultant hiring assignments.

  • Source and attract candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, databases and networking.

  • Conduct interviews and candidate assessments.

  • Present candidates and manage interview and offer processes.

  • Build and maintain talent pipelines within key disciplines.

  • Deliver an exceptional experience to both candidates and clients.

Business Development Responsibilities

  • Develop and grow customer relationships.

  • Identify new business opportunities and recruitment assignments.

  • Conduct client meetings and support commercial activities.

  • Build long-term partnerships and strategic accounts.

Who We Are Looking For

We believe you have:

  • Minimum 7 years of experience within recruitment, executive search, staffing or consultant hiring.

  • Proven experience managing full-cycle recruitment processes.

  • A strong professional network in Sweden.

  • Experience recruiting within Engineering, Energy, Infrastructure, Data Centers, IT, Industrial or Commercial functions is highly valued.

  • Excellent sourcing capabilities and experience using LinkedIn Recruiter.

  • Strong communication skills in Swedish and English.

  • A self-driven, entrepreneurial and delivery-focused mindset.

Success Factors

The ideal candidate will bring:

  • A strong personal and professional network.

  • High activity levels and a proactive approach.

  • Ability to build trust with both clients and candidates.

  • Strong recruitment delivery capabilities.

  • Commercial curiosity and an interest in growing into a broader 360 role over time.

What We Offer

  • Fully remote position with complete flexibility.

  • Commission-based compensation model with high earning potential.

  • Opportunity to join and shape a growing business in Sweden.

  • Support from SPERTON's global network and international delivery teams.

  • Modern recruitment tools and platforms.

  • Opportunity to develop into a full 360 Recruiter / Business Development Manager role.

  • The possibility to build a long-term career within an international and entrepreneurial organization.

Why Join SPERTON?

If you are an experienced recruiter who enjoys autonomy, thrives in an entrepreneurial environment and wants your earnings to reflect your performance, this is a unique opportunity to become part of an exciting growth journey and build something meaningful together with us.

Job Purpose: Industry-relevant instructor to steward a student-centric,

competency-based education experience.
Location: Remote, various locations throughout California

Salary Range: $75/hour

**The first review of applications shall occur on approximately 09/28/2026**

Position Overview

Under the supervision of the Department Chair of Business, the Adjunct Instructor plays a crucial role in fostering a competency-based learning environment that promotes social justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion. The Adjunct Instructor leverages Generative AI experience to instruct core concepts and skills customized and personalized to student learning. Integral to the role is the Adjunct Instructor’s ability to be responsive to a student’s unique needs and to continuously engage students early and often. Adjunct Instructors provide effective and substantive feedback that promotes mastery of program outcomes. Instructors provide guidance and encouragement and mentor students to be successful learners and workforce-ready.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities

The duties below are representative of the role and are not intended to cover all of the
duties performed within the scope of work.

  • Acts as a steward for carrying out Calbright’s mission and strategic vision by demonstrating effective and consistent commitment to equity-centered, competency-based education.
  • Provide consistent, timely, quality, substantive, and constructive feedback to students.
  • Monitors student progress and proactively offers support at key points of the student journey.
  • Provides expertise in Artificial Intelligence and maintains current knowledge in their field.
  • Fosters student learning through innovative, effective teaching practices.
  • Responds urgently to meet students' needs and communicates professionally and respectfully with students and all other members of the Calbright community.
  • Uses technology-based teaching and communication platforms to support students in developing competencies.
  • Collaborates with other professionals within the university to promote a positive, student-centric atmosphere.
  • Assess and validate student work based on mastery of industry skills and demonstration of knowledge.
  • Encourage student engagement with peers, the instructor, and the learning resources.
  • Appropriately document student engagement, outreach, and interventions.
  • Offer weekly office hours, web chats, or learning sessions.
  • Communicate with students using University-designated systems and through university-assigned email accounts.
  • Adhere to College policies and procedures, including the completion of mandatory training.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned that support the objective of the position.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Experience mentoring, training, or teaching adults
  • Expertise in Artificial Intelligence while maintaining currency in the field
  • Demonstrated ability to customize instructional support for adults with a variety of
    needs and educational backgrounds.
  • Strong understanding, adherence, and promotion of the tenets of Calbright’s competency-based education model.
  • Technological competency: Proficiency with Google Suite (or similar)
    applications, virtual instructional platforms, and collaboration tools.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present information concisely and accurately; friendly, persuasive speaking and writing style.
  • Extraordinary customer service orientation
  • Well organized - conscientious and thorough with detail.
  • Ability to use data to make decisions.
  • Demonstrate understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse
    academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability,
    and sexual orientation of community college students, staff, and faculty.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Cognitive Science
  • Demonstrated ability to work with diverse populations.
  • Ability to work a student-friendly schedule (evenings/weekends).

All candidates not holding the stated minimum degree qualifications, who are seeking consideration on the basis of equivalency, are required to submit a completed Equivalency Determination Request Form and must provide the supporting information and documentation.

Please usethis linkand download the Equivalency Determination Request form.

Candidates applying under the equivalency basis must submit this Equivalency Determination Request Form and documentation along with other materials specified on our Application page.

Desired Qualifications

  • Current Industry-aligned certification(s)
  • Online teaching experience
  • Interdisciplinary background
  • Experience applying social and emotional learning strategies with adult learners.

Working Conditions and Travel

  • Calbright College is a statewide online college where all instruction and support
    are done via various online technologies both in person and remotely. Calbright
    College has administrative offices in Sacramento available for use. When working remotely, employees should be able and willing to use digital communication tools as used by the college, and have the ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time.
  • Regular attendance is considered an essential job function; the inability to meet attendance requirements may preclude the employee from retaining employment.
  • The person holding this position is considered a mandated reporter under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in Calbright College policies, procedures, and Title IX.
  • Calbright College celebrates all forms of diversity and is deeply committed to fostering an inclusive environment within which students, staff, administrators, and faculty thrive. Individuals interested in advancing Calbright College’s strategic diversity goals are strongly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodations will be provided for qualified applicants with disabilities who self-disclose.
  • Requires the ability to function in a remote online instructional environment performing work of primarily a sedentary nature. Requires the ability to use hearing and speech to make presentations to groups and carry on conversations over the phone and in-person. Requires speaking skills to communicate with staff and students in one-on-one and small group settings, on the phone, and to distinguish sound prompts from various types of equipment. Requires near visual acuity to read printed materials and computer screens. Requires sufficient hand/arm/finger dexterity to retrieve work materials, operate a personal computer keyboard, and operate standard office equipment. Requires the ability to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Work is performed indoors where minimal safety considerations exist..

Equal Employment Opportunity

Calbright College provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Calbright College complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

Who We Are

Calbright College is one of California’s newest community colleges – the first statewide, online campus designed to bridge the gap between employers with unfilled positions and students who don’t have either the time or money to attend a traditional school. Our mission is to increase economic mobility and close equity gaps for working adults who lack easy access to traditional forms of higher education by offering online, flexible, affordable skills-based programs that provide tangible economic value for both working adults and hiring managers.

Bennett Aerospace, Inc., a subsidiary of Three Saints Bay, LLC, is seeking an Army National Guard Recruiting and Retention Subject Matter Expert to support the development of a competitive federal proposal.

This is a temporary, part-time consulting opportunity focused on helping our proposal team understand and respond to an Army National Guard requirement involving the Guard Strength Enhancement Program, Reserve Component transition counseling, recruiting and accession support, and related program management and help desk functions.

The selected SME will provide operational insight into how the ARNG identifies, counsels, processes, and tracks Soldiers transitioning from the Active Component, Army Reserve, and Individual Ready Reserve into ARNG units. The SME will help ensure our proposed technical, staffing, management, and quality-control approaches reflect how this work is performed in the field.

Responsibilities

  • Review the Performance Work Statement and related solicitation documents to identify operational requirements, risks, dependencies, and performance expectations.
  • Advise the proposal team on ARNG recruiting, retention, accession, and Reserve Component transition processes.
  • Explain the roles and working relationships among ARNG G1 organizations, Reserve Component Career Counselors, Transition Counselors, Recruiting and Retention Battalions, Interstate Transfer and In-Service Recruiting personnel, and gaining units.
  • Help develop an operational approach for the Guard Strength Enhancement Program and Active Component-to-Reserve Component transitions.
  • Provide insight into counseling Soldiers on ARNG and USAR opportunities, eligibility, benefits, incentives, entitlements, vacancies, assignments, and continued-service options.
  • Advise on the preparation, review, quality control, approval, and tracking of accession and transition packets.
  • Provide practical knowledge of relevant systems, including RETAIN, IPPS-A, iPERMS, MEDPROS, DPRO, AUVS, and related Army personnel systems.
  • Help identify appropriate labor categories, qualifications, staffing levels, workload assumptions, and organizational relationships.
  • Review proposed workflows for transition counseling, help desk support, system-access requests, production reporting, Soldier tracking, and issue resolution.
  • Assist in developing realistic performance metrics and quality-control methods for counseling, packet processing, accessions, customer support, reporting, and vacancy management.
  • Review proposal content for operational accuracy, completeness, and alignment with ARNG and Department of the Army policies and practices.
  • Participate in proposal strategy sessions, solution-development meetings, and draft reviews as needed.

Required Qualifications:

  • Former Army or Army National Guard service with substantial experience in recruiting, retention, career counseling, military personnel, strength management, or Reserve Component transition operations.
  • Direct knowledge of ARNG recruiting and retention processes and the accession of Soldiers into Army National Guard units.
  • Experience supporting Soldiers transitioning from the Active Component, Army Reserve, or Individual Ready Reserve.
  • Working knowledge of Army accession, reenlistment, assignment, vacancy, and personnel-readiness processes.
  • Familiarity with applicable Army and National Guard policies, including AR 601-280 and related accession and transition guidance.
  • Ability to translate operational experience into clear recommendations for proposal writers and business-development personnel.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Availability to support a time-sensitive proposal effort on a part-time consulting basis.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior service in an Army 79-series MOS, particularly 79T, 79S, 79V, or 79R.
  • Completion of the Reserve Component Transition NCO course or award of ASI 4R.
  • Experience serving as a Reserve Component Career Counselor, ARNG Recruiting and Retention NCO, Career Counselor, Transition Counselor, or ARNG G1 staff member.
  • Direct experience with the Guard Strength Enhancement Program.
  • Experience using RETAIN, IPPS-A, iPERMS, MEDPROS, DPRO, AUVS, or comparable Army personnel systems.
  • Experience processing or reviewing ARNG or USAR accession and transition packets.
  • Knowledge of ARNG strength-management, vacancy identification, incentives, Interstate Transfer, In-Service Recruiting, and Soldier assignment processes.
  • Prior experience supporting a federal proposal, performance work statement review, staffing solution, or technical approach development.
  • Experience overseeing geographically dispersed recruiting, retention, or transition-support personnel.

Position Details:

  • Employment Type: Temporary, part-time consultant
  • Location: Remote
  • Schedule: Flexible, based on proposal requirements and deadlines
  • Travel: Not anticipated
  • Clearance: Not required for proposal support
  • Duration: Through proposal submission, with the possibility of additional support during evaluations, discussions, or task-order development

raw.description:
Development Specialist
Washington

The Opportunity

Please consider joining our team! Reach Out and Read Northwest, an affiliate of the national Reach Out and Read program, reaches 200,000 families annually across Washington and Oregon, distributing over 330,000 books through 3,200 medical providers in over 400 clinics. Our focus is on serving underserved communities, where 62% of the children we reach are from low-income families, 42% identify as children of color, and 21% speak a home language other than English. Together, we contribute to the broader impact of the organization, which serves 4.6 million children across the country and distributes over 7.7 million books annually.

The Development Specialist is an early-career fundraising professional who brings strong writing and editing skills and thrives on collaboration. After an initial onboarding period, they will take on a significant share of our grant writing, drafting proposals and reports for review by the Associate Director of Development, while keeping deadlines on track, maintaining Salesforce data, and ensuring funders are thanked and stewarded well.

The Development Specialist reports to the Associate Director of Development and works closely with program team members coordinates with Regional Executive Director serving as an integrator who helps teams share information and meet funder commitments. As the Development Specialist grows in the role, they will have opportunities to take on more of the grant cycle, build relationships with funders, and develop their own portfolio over time.

Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Grant Writing and Reporting (50%)

  • Work alongside the Associate Director of Development to learn our programs, funders, and proposal library, then grow into drafting the majority of foundation and corporate proposals and reports

  • Write and edit grant proposals, adapting existing templates and boilerplate and translating program impact into clear, compelling, funder-aligned narratives

  • Coordinate the grant reporting process: gather program and financial information from colleagues, prepare drafts, and ensure interim and final reports are submitted accurately and on time

  • Maintain and update proposal templates, boilerplate language, and resource documents, including visually engaging materials created in Canva or similar tools

  • Support prospect research and funder qualification as requested

Grant Project Management and Collaboration (30%)

  • Manage the Northwest grants calendar, planning weeks ahead so applications, deliverables, and reports are on track well before deadlines

  • Track grant requirements, deliverables, and timelines in Asana, keeping teams informed and following up with the right colleagues for content and approvals

  • Help prepare agendas and materials for biweekly development team meetings

  • Enter and maintain grant and donor data in Salesforce, ensuring accuracy and alignment with National standards

  • Run recurring Salesforce reports, such as monthly or quarterly pipeline and grant status reports, to support team planning

  • Clearly communicate grant requirements and restrictions to leadership and finance, and submit backup materials promptly

Donor Stewardship and Acknowledgement (20%)

  • Facilitate donor and funder acknowledgment, ensuring gifts and grants are thanked promptly and personally

  • Prepare materials and briefings for stewardship and cultivation meetings led by the Associate Director of Development and Executive Director, and join select funder meetings to learn and inform upcoming proposals

About Reach Out and Read

Founded in 1989, Reach Out and Read is a national nonprofit organization working to ensure that all families have the opportunity to create meaningful everyday moments through shared reading aloud and relationship-building. By leveraging pediatric care to champion the positive effects of reading daily and distributing books, Reach Out and Read gives young children a foundation for success and reaches 4.6 million children across the country – half of whom identify as BIPOC and two-thirds of whom come from low-income families.

Reach Out and Read's tens of thousands of trained pediatric providers use books as a diagnostic tool during regular check-ups and teach parents how to engage their child with a book to promote positive parent-child interactions during the rapid brain growth between birth and age five. The daily practice of reading aloud with a parent supports children's literacy and math skill development, their social-emotional development, and prepares them for future success in school. Working together with our sites and providers, we leverage our three decades of expertise, build on our literacy foundations, and engage our shared networks as a catalyst for change, focusing on equitably strengthening and deepening our impact on the children, families, and communities we serve.

The Impact:

  • Reach Out and Read program sites are located in 6,500 clinics, safety net hospitals, medical systems, and other healthcare settings in all 50 states and the District of Columbia.

  • Reach Out and Read serves 4.6 million children and their families annually.

  • More than 7.7 million new, developmentally appropriate books are integrated into well-child visits with families annually.

  • 39,000 clinicians currently participate in Reach Out and Read.

  • Our peer-reviewed body of evidence demonstrates that Reach Out and Read parents are two-and-a-half times more likely to read regularly to their children, and that children experiencing Reach Out and Read show enhanced language development.
